0.long_answer: The subcutaneous lipoma nodule mentioned in the question is associated with the activation of Protein Kinase D2 (PKD2) by phorbol esters. Phorbol esters are known activators of certain kinases, including those in the protein kinase C family, but in this context, it has been highlighted that PKD2, when activated by phorbol esters, can efficiently phosphorylate substrates (such as histone H1) and contribute to the development of a painful lipoma nodule. The frequent low-level mutations observed in PKD2 further support its role in neoplastic processes, including the formation of such nodules.
